facts.fact: MyBroadband's table of Starlink status in African countries lists South Sudan as Available, dated 17 July 2026 (no South Sudan launch date or provider given; as_of is the article's table date).

TechnoMag lists South Sudan among 26 countries where Starlink is active now and gives a USD price of 50 a month Residential, 30 Residential Lite, kits 389 Standard and 200 Mini (as of mid-2026; as_of is the article's date).

note: NCA attended an African WRC-27 preparatory meeting on NGSO and D2D; no licence, sale or count stated for SSD.

slug: 2026-01-30 Can a digital economy exist in South Sudan without reliable DPI

facts.fact: Sudans Post says satellite internet such as Starlink has expanded access in select rural and conflict-affected areas of South Sudan and has offered relief to some businesses, NGOs and media organisations, but its cost puts it beyond most traders and households (as_of is the article date).

note: Only mention is an NCA-credited 'partnership with Starlink to expand rural connectivity'; no licence, launch, sale or subscriber count is stated.

facts.fact: Amnons Business Report says MTN South Sudan's Starlink partnership launched in September 2024 following approval from the National Communications Authority.
MTN South Sudan announced nationwide sale of Starlink kits and subscriptions through its customer service and Connect Stores.

systems.owner: SpaceX, sold by MTN South Sudan

facts.fact: Le Monde reports Starlink has been officially accessible in South Sudan since 22 August 2024, authorised by the authorities, with 1,300 terminals in use and four resellers approved by the NCA.
South Sudan's NCA says it granted Starlink a provisional licence and approved four tariff plans, with service preparing to launch.

note: No regulator subscriber count is stated.

facts.fact: South Sudan's National Communication Authority said a Satellite Landing Rights License and a Provisional Service License for Starlink were signed on 26 June 2024.

TechAfrica News carries MTN South Sudan's announcement that it sells and supports Starlink kits and subscriptions through its customer service points and Connect Stores nationwide, following a September 2024 partnership with Starlink and an authorisation by the National Communications Authority.

note: Starlink equipment was installed for one health facility; no licence or sale to households or businesses is stated.
Starlink is used as a facility link; no licence or sale to households or businesses is stated.
